# G10 Fulfillment to Celebrate Grand Opening of New Kenosha Distribution Facility with Ribbon-Cutting Ceremony

 Geneva10 

Sep 01, 2026, 08:34 ET

Mayor and Kenosha County Executive to join company and community leaders in marking the milestone expansion

KENOSHA, Wis., Sept. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- G10 Fulfillment, a North American third-party logistics and fulfillment provider, will hold a ribbon-cutting ceremony celebrating the grand opening of its new distribution facility in Kenosha, Wisconsin, on Thursday, September 10, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. at 12345 38th Street.

The new 315,000-square-foot facility replaces G10's former Twin Lakes location and more than doubles the company's Midwest warehouse capacity. Positioned along the Chicago–Milwaukee freight corridor, the site supports large-scale order fulfillment and regional inventory distribution as part of G10's broader logistics network.

Local officials will join G10 leadership to mark the occasion. Kenosha Mayor David Bogdala and Kenosha County Executive Samantha Kerkmam will offer remarks, with the Kenosha Area Business Alliance (KABA) serving as emcee for the event. Members of the media are welcome to attend.

"This facility represents a major step forward for our Midwest operations," said Mark Becker, CEO of G10 Fulfillment. "Doubling our capacity here in Kenosha allows us to support our retail partners with faster, more reliable fulfillment, and we're proud to be growing alongside a community that has been such a strong partner to our business."

About G10 Fulfillment

Founded in 2009, G10 Fulfillment has grown from a 10,000-square-foot airplane hangar into a multi-node logistics network across the United States. The company combines fulfillment technology with operational expertise to help retail and e-commerce brands—ranging from Walmart and Amazon to fast-growing Shopify companies—manage inventory, shipping and logistics across every sales channel, including regulated hazmat shipping, with speed, accuracy and consistency. For more information, visit https://g10fulfillment.com/.

#### New Kenosha hub significantly expands G10 Fulfillment’s Midwest warehouse capacity

 Posted in Kenosha County Economic Development 

A Delavan-based third-party logistics and fulfillment company has significantly expanded its Midwest warehouse capacity after moving into a new distribution facility in Kenosha.

G10 Fulfillment now occupies 315,000 square feet of a 600,000-square-foot building at 12345 38th St., just off Interstate 94. The move increases G10’s dock capacity to 65 doors from 30.

“The Midwest is probably the most important hub for us,” said co-founder and CEO Mark Becker, who was on hand Thursday for a ribbon-cutting at the facility. He pointed to the region’s freight infrastructure and its location along the trucking corridor between Chicago and Milwaukee.

Becker said the facility can handle nearly 7 acres of inventory under one roof. G10 shares the building with food manufacturer Eagle Foods.

G10 invested about $2 million in the Kenosha buildout, which Becker said covered racking, automation and staffing costs.

The facility has about 100 workers, a figure he expects to reach 150 by March 2027. Seasonal hiring could push employment toward 200 during the Black Friday peak before tapering in January.

#### G10’s real estate

The move consolidates two smaller warehouses — a 150,000-square-foot building in Twin Lakes and a 50,000-square-foot site in New Berlin — into one operation.

G10 is giving up both former buildings rather than keeping them as backup capacity, according to the chief executive. The company owns the Twin Lakes site, which is being leased to Allied Plastics. The New Berlin property is owned by one of Becker’s business partners and is being turned over to another venture.

Kenosha will be one of three anchor hubs in G10’s national network, he said, alongside a Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, warehouse scheduled to open in October and a planned Ontario, Canada, facility targeted for 2027.

The company is also exploring a location in Southern California.

G10 has grown from a 10,000-square-foot hangar in Lake Geneva in 2009 into a fulfillment operation that stores, processes and ships products for manufacturers and brands across multiple sales channels.

Source: Courtesy of Maersk

Maersk is investing $100 million in a new fulfillment center in Hopedale, Massachusetts, creating about 1,000 jobs and expanding Northeast delivery capacity.

 By 24/7 Staff July 16, 2026 

Maersk will open a new 617,000-square-foot fulfillment center in Hopedale, Massachusetts, later this summer, investing $100 million in the project and creating approximately 1,000 jobs.

The facility will become part of Maersk's North American contract logistics network and will work with a major e-commerce customer. At full capacity, the site is expected to process up to 330,000 units a day while expanding the company's fulfillment and delivery network across the Northeast.

The Hopedale facility marks one of Maersk's larger recent investments in U.S. logistics infrastructure as retailers and brands continue placing inventory closer to customers to speed deliveries.

“We are seeing continued customer demand for modern fulfillment capabilities,” said Dave Hune, Head of Maersk Contract Logistics North America. “Our investment in Hopedale reflects continued customer demand for modern fulfillment capabilities and reinforces Maersk's commitment to building resilient, scalable supply chains across North America.”

## Built for high-volume e-commerce

The fulfillment center is equipped with automated conveyor and sortation systems designed to handle large volumes of orders. Maersk said the operation will process up to 330,000 units per day during peak periods.

The site will serve a single large-scale e-commerce customer, although Maersk did not identify the company.

Hiring is already underway for leadership, warehouse, and support positions ahead of the facility's opening later this summer.

## Expanding Maersk's Northeast network

The new operation expands Maersk's contract logistics network in North America and strengthens its presence in the Northeast.

The company said many customers are looking to position inventory closer to consumers to reduce delivery times while improving order fulfillment.

The Hopedale facility combines warehousing, fulfillment, and distribution within Maersk's broader logistics network, which includes ocean shipping, trucking, air freight, and inland transportation.

The company said the investment will help it keep up with customer growth while expanding its fulfillment network in one of the country's largest consumer markets.

# Maersk Commits US$100m to New Hopedale Fulfillment Center, Advancing Integrated Logistics Push in the US Northeast

Maersk, the global integrator of container logistics operating across more than 130 countries, is deepening its footprint in North American contract logistics with a US$100m investment in a new fulfillment center in Hopedale, Massachusetts. The 617,000-square-foot facility is scheduled to open in late August 2026, positioning the company to strengthen fulfillment capacity for cargo owners across the region.

Built around the requirements of a single major e-commerce customer, the site will function as a central node in Maersk’s contract logistics network throughout the US Northeast. The project also carries substantial employment implications. Close to 1,000 positions — spanning leadership, operations, and support functions — are being filled, with hiring already underway. For the surrounding community, the scale of new employment represents a meaningful economic contribution.

For shippers, the Hopedale centre signals more than added warehouse space. It reinforces Maersk’s broader strategy to unify transportation, warehousing, fulfilment, and distribution into a single integrated logistics proposition for North American customers — an approach designed to reduce hand-off friction, tighten delivery reliability, and give cargo owners greater visibility and control across the supply chain.

## Facilities in Arizona and Missouri Expand Capacity for Customers and Strengthen XPO’s North American Network

 October 01, 2026 07:45 ET | Source: XPO, Inc. 

GREENWICH, Conn., Oct. 01, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- XPO (NYSE: XPO), a leading provider of freight transportation in North America, today announced the opening of two new service centers in Mesa, Arizona, and Cameron, Missouri. The facilities expand XPO’s capacity to meet growing freight demand in the Phoenix and Kansas City metropolitan areas. Matt Carroll, president of XPO’s West Division, said, “These new service centers deepen our presence in two critical freight markets and reflect our strategic approach to investing in our network. We’ve added capacity where our customers need it most, positioning us to support their growth while delivering the world-class service they count on.” The 51,000-square-foot Mesa facility has 86 dock doors and a team of more than 100 employees. Located in one of the nation’s largest and fastest-growing metropolitan areas, it complements XPO’s existing Phoenix service center, adding capacity to meet increasing freight demand fueled by industrial investment and cross-border trade with Mexico. The 13,000-square-foot Cameron service center has 32 dock doors and a team of more than 30 employees. Located at the intersection of two major highways, I-35 and U.S. 36, it enables more efficient freight movement along key north-south and east-west freight corridors in the Midwest. XPO has opened nearly 35 new service centers across the country since 2021, expanding its network dock door capacity by 15%. Construction at the Mesa and Cameron sites was completed this summer, and their openings bring XPO’s North American network to 300 service centers, which provide direct service to 99% of U.S. ZIP codes and cross-border service to and from Canada and Mexico. The company’s customer-focused organization efficiently moves 16 billion pounds of freight per year, enabled by its proprietary technology. XPO serves 55,000 customers with 586 locations and 38,000 employees in North America and Europe, and is headquartered in Greenwich, Conn., USA. Buena Park, CA, Sept. 11, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- States Logistics Services, Inc. today announced plans to establish a Las Vegas distribution center, extending its network across the Western United States. The move positions the company to serve one of the fastest growing logistics hubs in the region, with direct access to Southern California, Arizona, Utah, Nevada, and the broader Mountain West.

The planned Las Vegas distribution center is designed to give customers greater flexibility in how they move and store product, reducing transportation costs, shortening transit times, and strengthening supply chain resilience across the region. For States Logistics, it marks a strategic step in a network built to grow alongside the brands it serves.
...
States Logistics is targeting food and beverage, consumer packaged goods, retail and e-commerce, and health and wellness brands with the planned Las Vegas distribution center, along with importers, manufacturers, and companies looking to diversify beyond a Southern California footprint. The company is building awareness ahead of the location becoming operational, encouraging both current customers and prospective ones to start the conversation early.

For existing customers, the Las Vegas distribution center will add another strategic node to the States Logistics network, giving brands more flexibility in inventory placement and a more resilient, scalable supply chain, all while maintaining the same level of service they already count on. For companies evaluating a new logistics partner, the move signals States Logistics’ continued investment in infrastructure, technology, and long-term customer success.

Once operational, the Las Vegas distribution center will bring the same food-grade expertise, technology, and hands-on service that has made States Logistics a trusted 3PL partner across California and Arizona since 1958, now extended into one of the country’s most important logistics markets.
...
